title: CeeDee Lamb injury update as Cowboys star WR exits vs. Buccaneers
description: The Dallas Cowboys may have lost one of their top pass-catching weapons in their Week 5 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys may have lost one of their top pass-catching weapons in their Week 5 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

CeeDee Lamb is dealing with a quad injury. He was deemed "questionable" to return to the game, according to Amazon's sideline reporter Kaylee Hartung, when Dallas began a drive with 8:32 remaining in regulation.

Lamb briefly returned to the field for a play after Hartung's report. However, he was seen hobbling off the field shortly after the play.

It wasn't immediately clear when Lamb suffered the injury. He did return to the field for the 2-point conversion attempt, so his status moving forward will bear monitoring.

Here's more to know about Lamb's status moving forward.

The Cowboys did not immediately provide an update about Lamb's status.

Lamb caught just two passes for nine yards before exiting the game and then eventually returning.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: CeeDee Lamb injury update as Cowboys star WR exits vs. Buccaneers

title: Cowboys close to within 24-16 on George Pickens' TD as CeeDee Lamb is questionable to return
description: The Cowboys are without wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, who is questionable to return with a quad injury.
fullText:
The Cowboys are without wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, who is questionable to return with a quad injury. They still have George Pickens, though.

His 17-yard touchdown reception has drawn the Cowboys to within one score of the Bucs.

Dallas went for 2 points and Dak Prescott's pass was incomplete, leaving the Cowboys trailing 24-16 with 5:26 left.

The Cowboys got a break when Todd Bowles decided to go for it on fourth-and-goal from the Dallas 1 with 8:36 remaining. Sean Tucker was stopped for no gain by Jaishawn Barham, giving the Cowboys hope.

They then drove 99 yards in 10 plays.

The Bucs list left tackle Tristan Wirfs questionable to return with cramps.

title: Cowboys ripped for 'awful' defensive effort vs. Buccaneers
description: The Cowboys' defensive concerns only worsened against the winless Buccaneers.
fullText:
Cowboys ripped for 'awful' defensive effort vs. Buccaneers originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

No one would've said the Cowboys' defense was a strength through the first four weeks of the season, but Dallas appeared to be sitting pretty ahead of a home "Thursday Night Football" matchup against a reeling Buccaneers squad.

Tampa Bay entered Thursday winless and down to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels at quarterback with Baker Mayfield injured. Daniels largely struggled to sustain drives in his first start, so the idea that he could keep up with a high-flying Dallas offense seemed far-fetched.

The Cowboys' defense, however, had other ideas. Dallas struggled to contain Tampa Bay's previously anemic offense, and fan frustration boiled up after a series of lapses in a 24-16 loss.

Here's a look at the Cowboys' continued defensive struggles and the best reactions.

MORE:Why Joey Porter Jr. was inactive in surprise decision

The Cowboys couldn't get the Buccaneers' offense off the field in the first half, as Tampa Bay — aided by three penalties — put together a marathon drive spanning nearly 11 minutes and ending in a Bucky Irving touchdown.

After a stronger finish to the first half, the unit had a number of miscues in the third quarter. Irving broke free for a 72-yard run that set up an Emeka Egbuka rushing touchdown, and the defense soon allowed Tez Johnson to get wide open for a 64-yard gain that set up another score.

Tez Johnson is WIDE open for another Bucs big gain! @TBvsDAL on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus https://t.co/yilGqjeFzj

After a special teams mistake gave the Buccaneers' offense another opportunity, Dallas let Daniels and Egbuka convert a third-and-21 to keep the drive alive and ultimately put three more points on the board.

Jalon Daniels connects with Emeka Egbuka to convert the 3rd and 21! @TBvsDAL on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus https://t.co/mUlIG4zkh0

When the Cowboys had a chance to get the Buccaneers off the field later on, Shavon Revel Jr., filling in for an ill Joey Porter Jr., was called for pass interference on third-and-13.

Fans and pundits were understandably frustrated:

This is more about the Dallas Cowboys being pretenders, not contenders, once again. This defense is AWFUL. Bucs are making them pay #WeAreTheKrewe

The Cowboys front office and coaching staff are lying to themselves if they believe this defense is improved.

I know what this is saying, but I sort of think this might be one of the worst quarters of Cowboys football that I have ever seen.

This is one of the lowest points for the Dallas Cowboys in the Brian Schottenheimer era, and that is really saying something. He and his whole staff look overwhelmed and like they have no business operating an NFL team. This is ugly and they are the reason why.

MORE:How Buccaneers' longest drive in 19 years baffled Cowboys

Some directed their ire toward defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who is only five games into his tenure.

The Cowboys might seriously want to think about moving on from Christian Parker sooner rather than later. Zero signs that this is going to get better.

Christian Parker is no different than Matt Eberflus.

Here's a look at how the Cowboys defense stacks up so far in 2026.

Here's where the Cowboys' defense ranked among all teams coming into Thursday's game:

Dallas is the only team without a defensive interception and was already allowing nearly 400 yards per game before Thursday's contest.

While the Cowboys' defense wasn't necessarily bludgeoned by the Buccaneers, the mistakes and lapses were fairly stunning considering the way Tampa Bay's offense had been struggling coming into the night.

title: Trump hosts awards party for tech billionaires, almost as if he doesn’t care about ordinary Americans
description:
Amid a cost-of-living crisis, with US midterms a month away, the president held a ceremony to celebrate our tech overlords – again
He stands accused of being out of touch, enriching himself and his family, building a lavish White House ballroom and, with elections looming, neglecting the hardships of the voters who brought him to power.
Time for Donald Trump to show he still has the common touch? Nope.
 Continue reading...
fullText:
Amid a cost-of-living crisis, with US midterms a month away, the president held a ceremony to celebrate our tech overlords – again

He stands accused of being out of touch, enriching himself and his family, building a lavish White House ballroom and, with elections looming, neglecting the hardships of the voters who brought him to power.

Time for Donald Trump to show he still has the common touch? Nope.

On Thursday, the US president went to a building he named after himself, dished out awards to the world’s richest person – his old frenemy Elon Musk – and other tech billionaires and even received an award that belonged to his late uncle.

Given Trump’s gold fetish, the event was naturally entitled the Golden Age of American Innovation summit, which will be news to the many agencies and academies suffering billions of dollars in cuts to scientific research on his watch.

“We have an extremely high-IQ audience for a change,” the president told about 300 invited guests at the Donald J Trump Institute of Peace in Washington, a compliment he never pays to the crowds who line up for hours to attend his campaign rallies.

Standing on a podium with a white backdrop and series of US flags, the president gave a perfunctory speech, sticking unusually close to his teleprompter. He made references to artificial super intelligence but steered clear of the datacentres these tech overlords are erecting all over the country and, in the process, achieving the unique feat of getting Democrats and Republicans to agree on how much they hate them.

Michael Kratsios, director of the White House office of science and technology policy, then treated Trump to a video about his uncle, Dr John Trump, an electrical engineer and professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology who received the National Medal of Science in 1983.

The short film’s claims that John Trump’s research produced X-ray generators “used for the first radiation treatments for cancer” and that “his radars jammed German defences” on D-day in 1944 owe something to his nephew’s fondness for “truthful hyperbole”.

Six years ago, the president, who believes in “good genes” and “racehorse theory”, suggested that his uncle’s legacy would help him fight the Covid-19 pandemic: “He was a great super genius. Dr John Trump. I like this stuff. I really get it. People are surprised that I understand it. Every one of these doctors said: ‘How do you know so much about this?’ Maybe I have a natural ability. Maybe I should have done that instead of running for president.”

Kratsios had a surprise for the boss. He presented Trump with his uncle’s National Medal of Science in a handsome frame as the audience clapped. He looked happy enough, though it was clear this won’t displace the gaudy Fifa peace prize from his trophy cabinet.

Among the six tech leaders who came up on stage to receive an award for scientific and technological achievement, five were immigrants.

The “America first” president gave the National Medal of Science to SpaceX chief executive Musk (born in South Africa); Google co-founder Sergey Brin (Russia); Jensen Huang (Taiwan), whose AI chip maker Nvidia is the world’s most valuable company; and Lisa Su (Taiwan), head of the semiconductor company Advanced Micro Devices.

Trump also handed the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to Microsoft supremo Satya Nadella (India) and Dell Technologies chief executive Michael Dell (Texas). Hours earlier, JD Vance had announced Microsoft’s suspension from a programme allowing companies to sponsor foreign workers for green cards.

The trillionaire Musk was wearing a dark suit, white shirt and white tie. Trump gave him a pat on the back, handed him the medal and gave him another pat, then showed him a certificate and patted him once more. In earlier remarks, the president called Musk an “industrial titan”, “brilliant engineer”, “national treasure” and “modern-day Thomas Edison”. He observed: “It all works out well for Elon, right?”

These guys’ relationship is more complicated than Rhett Butler and Scarlett O’Hara. Musk helped buy the 2024 election for Trump and found Doge a useful vehicle to gut the federal agencies investigating his companies. The president considered Musk’s Grok chatbot ingenious after it accurately predicted that ordinary Venezuelans would celebrate the removal of leader Nicolás Maduro, according to Time magazine.

Then came their explosive falling out, with Musk tweeting on his own X platform: “Time to drop the really big bomb: [Trump] is in the Epstein files. That is the real reason they have not been made public.” It turned out both men were in the files.

Vance reportedly brokered a truce between the two titanic egos. The bromance has never been fully rekindled, but Thursday was proof that power and wealth can’t live without each other – especially with elections less than a month away and Trump’s approval rating in the doldrums.

When the ceremony was over, however, it was AI king Huang who remained on stage alongside Trump as the familiar strains of the Village People’s YMCA blasted from loudspeakers (“Young man, when you’re short on your dough,” did not resonate with this crowd). The pair were pointing and directing people, presumably for a photo op, and looking pleased with themselves. It was a fitting closing image of two men who rule the world and may yet find a artificial super intelligent way to destroy it.

title: Firmus pulls biggest ASX float since Telstra amid investor doubt about datacentre company
description: The $11-a-share offer would have been the biggest debut on the stock market since the telecommunication giant in...
fullText:
The $11-a-share offer would have been the biggest debut on the stock market since the telecommunication giant in 1997

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Firmus Technologies has scrapped what was set to be Australia’s biggest company listing in decades after investor demand for its much-hyped AI datacentre business failed to materialise.

A Firmus spokesperson said the board decided that proceeding with the offer was no longer in the best interests of the company and its shareholders.

“Firmus will now pursue capital from the private markets and consider alternative public and private market options,” the spokesperson said on Friday morning.

“We will provide additional information to shareholders as those options progress.”

Firmus, with an anticipated $44bn valuation, was expected to be the biggest ASX listing since Telstra in 1997.

But it faced mounting scepticism over its huge valuation, and forecast earnings, for a company in its startup phase with just two, small operational sites.

Backed by chip maker Nvidia and Wall Street firms Blackstone, Jane Street and Coatue, Firmus’s backers believed they could raise billions of dollars by selling shares in a public float with the help of five brokers.

The lack of demand means Firmus will need to raise money from private investors to fund its plans to build liquid-cooled “AI factories” in Australia and across Asia.

The polished Firmus pitch started to unravel midweek after it became clear the company’s bankers had vastly overestimated demand in their bid to raise $7bn from investors ahead of listing on the ASX on 23 October.

This prompted discussions about a heavy reduction in the company’s proposed $11-a-share initial public offering, according to one investment manager briefed on the matter.

The company ultimately decided to withdraw its application to list on the ASX altogether.

Guardian Australia previously reported growing concern that early Firmus investors were going to use retail investors buying into the float as their “exit strategy”, leaving small investors exposed if the excitement dissipated.

The datacentre company’s troubles have already rattled other parts of the market, with shares in Firmus investor Maas Group plunging more than 20% on Thursday.

The anticipated financial worth of the founders – Oliver Curtis, his cousin Tim Rosenfield, and Curtis’s former brother-in-law Jonathan Levee – will also be greatly reduced.

title: The flu sidelines James Talarico at a crucial moment in the Texas Senate race
description:
Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico has been off the campaign trail, sick with the flu. (Bill Clark / CQ-Roll Call via Getty)
The bitter fight over a Texas Senate seat that Democrats believe is within reach for the first time in decades should be ramping up right now.
But in the final push, when campaigns believe most voters are finally tuning in, Democratic state Rep. James Talarico has been off the trail for in-person events in the state for 12 days. 
His campaign says he has the flu and is expected to be back in action this weekend.
fullText:
The bitter fight over a Texas Senate seat that Democrats believe is within reach for the first time in decades should be ramping up right now.

But in the final push, when campaigns believe most voters are finally tuning in, Democratic state Rep. James Talarico has been off the trail for in-person events in the state for 12 days.

His campaign says he has the flu and is expected to be back in action this weekend.

While he has appeared virtually at a forum, Talarico’s last in-person event in the state was on Sept. 26. He visited New York on Sept. 29 for a private fundraiser, and, according to the virtual remarks he gave to the Hispanic Business Council the next day, he returned to Dallas and visited urgent care.

It has all prompted a stream of fodder from his opponent, Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, whose campaign is calling on Talarico to produce a photo of himself with a newspaper showing today’s date.

“We have a simple request: proof of life,” Paxton campaign spokeswoman Madison Cercy said. “James Talarico wants to represent 31 million Texans in the U.S. Senate, but for 12 days, he’s hidden from every one of them. There’s a reason they call it ‘Texas Tough,’ and it’s not because Texans hide at the first sign of trouble. If James Talarico is too fragile to face Texans, he has no business asking for their vote.”

While some Texas Democrats are shrugging it off, it is causing some consternation.

“He’s, like, really sick. Believe me, we don’t want this right now,” a Texas Democrat involved in the Talarico race said. “We’d rather have him on the trail.”

At the Hispanic Business Council event, Talarico appeared virtually and was blowing his nose and coughing through the event.

“I was starting to feel kind of under the weather a few days ago, and last night it got so bad that I went to the urgent care here in Dallas, and I was diagnosed with the flu,” Talarico said at the time. “I’m running a fever, and I’m my most contagious right now. And I guess I’ve been shaking too many hands on the campaign trail, and so I want to keep everybody safe.”

Talarico’s absence is undoubtedly a curveball for Democrats who believe his best asset is connecting with potential voters in person. It is also a turnaround for Talarico, who had been visible in the early days of the campaign as Paxton was off the trail.

“After holding more than 100 public events and shaking tens of thousands of hands, James came down with the flu but will be back on the trail this weekend,” Talarico spokesman JT Ennis said in a statement. “Ken Paxton has been ignoring Texans this entire campaign, and his priorities are clear: he doesn’t answer to the people of this state — he answers to his billionaire megadonors and special interests.”

Democratic political strategist Ed Espinoza said some supporters he has spoken to noted Talarico’s absence from in-person campaign events and lamented that they wanted to make sure other people were seeing enough of him.

Espinoza, though, said he didn’t think that would be a problem.

“Look, he’s got, like, $80 million of ads going right now. So I think that’s pretty good scale for him at the moment,” Espinoza said. “He may be recovering at home, but he is still everywhere.”

Espinoza said he’d rather Talarico be off the trail and recovering now rather than be hampered even closer to the election.

Texas Democratic Party Chair Kendall Scudder said Paxton “caught a little bit of a break” with Talarico’s absence.

“It’s certainly not ideal, but we want to make sure he does everything he needs to to make sure that he’s healthy and ready to go. We’re in the homestretch, and it sounds like he’s on the mend, and that’s great news,” Scudder said. “He’s a phenomenal candidate, he’s been working really hard for a long time, and everyone gets sick every now and then.”

To Talarico’s great fortune, distractions have abounded. A steady flow of damaging audio featuring Paxton saying that President Donald Trump’s midterm convention wasn’t helpful or that cuts to “mandatory spending” were inevitable has grabbed public attention.

At the same time, both Paxton and Trump have hit Talarico for being off the trail.

“You haven’t seen him in a couple of weeks,” Trump said Wednesday at a rally in San Antonio. “I hear the guy has disappeared. Nobody knows. You know where he is? He’s sick, because he’s forced to eat meat for political reasons and he’s throwing up all over the place.”

After the rally, Trump posted a demand on social media that Talarico show up in person to debate Paxton.

“He should immediately report to a Debate Stage against Ken Paxton, who is ready, willing, and able, one of the best Attorney Generals in the Country, and will soon be, hopefully, a United States Senator representing the Great People of Texas!” Trump said on Truth Social.

It was a twist, given that Talarico has repeatedly called on Paxton to debate. Though he’s not on the trail yet, Talarico did respond over social media:

“President Trump just said Ken Paxton should debate,” Talarico wrote. “I agree. Ball’s in your court @KenPaxtonTX.”

title: Man hospitalized in New York shooting involving federal agents, NYPD says
description:
US immigration agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday in his car with a child present in the ‌Marble Hill neighborhood of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitnesses.

fullText:
NEW YORK, Oct 8 (Reuters) - US immigration agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday in his car with a child present in the ‌Marble Hill neighborhood of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitnesses.

"Early ‌reports indicate agents surrounded (the man) and a 5-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds," New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani ​said in a statement.

The mayor said the child was believed to have been physically unharmed.

"This is an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation," Mamdani said, adding he planned to speak to President Donald Trump and "demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city. I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorize our communities."

The ‌Department of Homeland Security, ICE's parent ⁠agency, said in a statement ICE officers were conducting a "targeted enforcement operation" in the Bronx, New York, to arrest a man from the Dominican Republic with a ⁠prior criminal conviction.

"During the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon and the criminal illegal alien was injured," DHS said, adding that ICE officers rendered immediate aid. "The individual is alive and at a local hospital."

The shooting occurred ​at ​around 4 p.m. ET (2000 GMT), DHS said.

Working at a ​restaurant near the shooting, Pedro Almarez said ‌he heard shots fired and went outside to see several officers wearing ICE attire at the scene.

"There were a lot of ICE officers, three or four cars," Almarez told Reuters by phone, adding the man who was shot appeared to be between 20 and 30 years of age. He said NYPD officers arrived about 10 minutes later. He said the man was only removed from his car after an ‌ambulance arrived.

At the shooting scene, where police strung yellow crime-scene ​tape to cordon off a city block, a woman standing ​on a balcony overlooking the area told officers ​they were "taking our children," according to a Reuters witness.

Federal immigration agents have shot ‌at least 21 people since Republican President Donald ​Trump returned to office, ​7 fatally, sparking protests across the US. Critics contend that Trump's push to ramp up deportations has led to an increasing number of violent confrontations, and accuse the administration of resisting ​accountability for the agents involved.

fullText:
State health authorities are urging people enrolled in Medicaid to check whether they will remain eligible when new rules kick in that could leave millions of Americans without access.

From Jan. 1, Medicaid beneficiaries in dozens of states will have to work, study or volunteer for at least 80 hours a month or meet a minimum income requirement to keep their coverage, among a series of new rules due to take effect.

Many who are still eligible for the program risk losing coverage because of the "added paperwork" and "the hoops you have to jump through," Nate Crippes, a lawyer at the Disability Law Center in Utah, told the Associated Press.

The Congressional Budget Office estimated in October 2025 that the new work requirement alone would leave about 5.3 million more people uninsured by 2034.

A group of 25 Democratic-led states and the District of Columbia sued to temporarily block the rules in June, saying it unlawfully narrowed exemptions for people with serious medical conditions. A federal judge denied the request in July.

The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS), the federal agency that administers the program, said in June that the changes were designed to promote "economic stability, self-sufficiency, and independence," and that they would help Americans build skills through work, education, job training or community service.

Nevada, North Carolina and Pennsylvania are among the states that have issued guidance. Pennsylvania has urged residents to update their contact information and check whether they qualify for an exemption, as it mails notices to more than 700,000 expansion enrollees.

Nebraska began rolling out the changes in May, Montana in July and Iowa will follow in December. Montana's grace period ended on Oct. 1, so enrollees there can now lose coverage for not complying.

Here's what to know about what the new requirements are, who is exempt, how people can prove they qualify and what paperwork they'll need to keep their Medicaid coverage.

Starting Jan. 1, 2027, 40 states and D.C. will be required to introduce a work and community engagement requirement for adults covered by Medicaid's expansion to low-income adults — people ages 19 to 64 who are not pregnant and not enrolled in Medicare. In 2025, about 20 million of the 82.4 million people enrolled in Medicaid were in that group.

Children, adults aged 65 and over and people who qualify through a disability or as low-income parents are not covered by the new rules.

Enrollees in that group will need to work, be enrolled in school at least half-time, take part in a work program or volunteer for at least 80 hours a month. These activities can be combined to reach the monthly total, the federal rules say.

They can also meet the requirement through income alone, earning the equivalent of 80 hours on the federal minimum wage — at least $580 a month in 2026. Income can count money from other people in the household, or from outside a job such as unemployment benefits.

Rather than telling the state each month that they have met those requirements, enrollees will be required to prove that they met them for at least one month before the month they apply. This is also the case at renewal — which will take place twice a year — when existing enrollees must show they met it for one or more months between renewals. Some states, like New Hampshire and Indiana, have chosen to check more often.

States have to check the records they already have first, like wage and unemployment data, SNAP and TANF files, Medicaid claims and school enrollment, before asking anyone for proof. Applications and renewal forms will include new questions and, in a few states, a separate portal for people to prove they meet these criteria.

If a state cannot verify someone from its own data, it must send a notice of noncompliance, which must be answered within 30 days or its coverage ends. That notice has to explain how to show compliance or exemption, and how to reapply if they lose coverage.

Enrollees are exempt from meeting the requirement if they fall into one of these groups:

medically frail, or have medical needs that significantly impair their ability to comply

a parent, guardian or caregiver of a child age 13 or younger, or of a disabled person

a veteran with a total disability rating

Native American and Alaska Native people

in a drug or alcohol treatment program

already meeting TANF work rules, or in a household receiving SNAP without a SNAP exemption

Those who are medically frail are facing significant changes. States must first look at 12 months of a person's Medicaid claims to determine if a person is medically frail. The condition must significantly impair a person's ability to work, study or volunteer.

That 12-month history will not exist for someone applying for the first time, and may be thin for anyone who enrolled only recently. Those are the people most likely to be asked to prove it themselves.

When the records cannot settle it, the new rules let states accept an enrollee's own account of their condition until the end of 2027. Starting in 2028, they can do that only once during a period of enrollment.

After that, states must request documentation, which could include a doctor's certification, medical records, a disability award letter or a provider form. States cannot end someone's coverage solely because paperwork does not exist or cannot reasonably be obtained.

The requirement applies in the 40 states and the District of Columbia that expanded Medicaid to low-income adults.

In at least six states — Arkansas, Idaho, Indiana, New Hampshire, North Carolina and Ohio — enrollees will have to provide documentation that they are medically frail rather than simply self-report, according to ABC News.

Ten states never expanded Medicaid, and in six of those nobody is affected, because the group the requirement targets was never eligible there. The exceptions are Georgia, South Carolina, Tennessee and Wisconsin, which cover some low-income adults through waivers and whose enrollees are caught by the new rules.

title: Arizona candidate says she felt like a 'hypocrite' for not speaking up about reported rape
description:

"I was talking to some seniors about fighting for reinstating and funding the [Veterans Administration] and fixing Social Security, actually addressing the issues" amid federal government cuts or healthcare changes that impacted them, Greene-Placentia told ABC News Live anchor Kyra Phillips.

fullText:
Bernadette Greene-Placentia said is speaking out for sexual assault survivors.

Bernadette Greene-Placentia, a Democratic candidate for Congress who said she was raped while fixing a campaign sign in August, told ABC News on Thursday that she was motivated to speak up because of the arguments she was making on the campaign trail.

"I was talking to some seniors about fighting for reinstating and funding the [Veterans Administration] and fixing Social Security, actually addressing the issues" amid federal government cuts or healthcare changes that impacted them, Greene-Placentia told ABC News Live anchor Kyra Phillips.

"It just crossed my mind at that point -- like, wow, I'm kind of being a hypocrite because I'm saying I'm going to fight for Arizonans. I'm going to fight for these folks, but I'm not fighting for women who've been victims of sexual assault, and that's just not how I was raised," she said. "So afterwards, I told my husband and my team, I was like, this is really going to suck, but I have to speak up."

Greene-Placentia, a former truck driver who is running in the state's 8th District to try to unseat Republican Rep. Abe Hamadeh, told Phoenix New Times, a local news outlet, in a story published Wednesday that she was attacked around 2 a.m. as she was walking toward a campaign sign in a parking lot north of Phoenix. She said she had been subdued and then woke up to find that she was being raped by an unknown assailant.

Greene-Placentia told the news outlet she reported the assault to the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office, which confirmed to ABC News that a report was filed on Aug. 31 and that there is an ongoing investigation, but said the office could not comment further on the investigation.

She told ABC News on Thursday that she thinks it was a "crime of opportunity" and that she was not necessarily targeted, but she mentioned that her face is on campaign signs and "I'm pretty sure they knew who I was. Whether it was for political reasons or whatever, I mean, it was an attack on a woman, and no woman should be targeted, regardless of whether it's for political reasons or just because they're predators."

It hadn't initially worried her to go out so late to fix campaign signs.

"I mean, I have about 4 million miles across the country, and, you know, I've learned how to take care of myself ... it's just easier to do it [fix signs] at night. And usually I would go out with my husband or a staffer or a volunteer. But if I saw one that was just hanging by the rebar or somethin. ... I never heard [the attacker] coming," she said.

"And it's frustrating to me because I like to think I have pretty good situational awareness, but obviously when someone deliberately sneaking up on you, it's hard to defend yourself."

Greene-Placentia said she does not remember coming home and has little memory of the next day, although said there is video of her landlord in the driveway.

"She saw me standing out there, and I guess I was just literally, like, staring off into space or something. And she's like, Bernadette, Bernadette, are you Ok? Are you Ok? And I just looked, you know, horrible."

She said she did not say anything to her campaign staff at first, and took a few days before she told her husband.

Asked what she wants voters to know about her in addition to her taking her story to Capitol Hill, Green-Placentia told ABC News she wants voters, including survivors of sexual assault, to know she was going to "fight" for them.

"I want people to know that I'm going to stand up. I'm going to fight for you. I'm going to fight for everybody because -- I got into politics, I gave up a career I loved, because I felt like there weren't people like me, like the average American," she said.

"Our voices were not being represented, and that's from the working class. That's from women that have been victims of sexual assault. That's our seniors, our veterans, our teachers, and they need to know that they have somebody that lives the same life they do, that has shared experiences, and will take that to D.C. and represent them fairly, transparently."

She also said she understands where women who don't speak up about being assaulted are coming from, even though she used to be someone who was more judgmental of people who shared their stories.

She brought up the 2018 hearings where professor Christine Blasey Ford accused then-Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh of sexual assault. Kavanaugh emphatically denied the allegations and was eventually confirmed to the court.

"I am a little ashamed to admit that I was one of those people. You know, like during the Kavanaugh hearings, for example, I was like, 'Why did she wait so long? If he was out doing this to her, he's going to do it to somebody else.' But let me tell you, that is so hard to acknowledge to yourself that somebody took your power away from you, that they stripped you of your bodily autonomy, and you know overpowered you with physical strength, and you don't want to admit that."

She added, "I was a truck driver. I was tough. I was in a male-dominated industry as an owner-operator and built up a small fleet. You know, how could I let this happen to me? I didn't want anybody to know. I just wanted to move on, and I can certainly understand why women don't want to tell that their story or what happened. But I also realized that as long as I don't say anything, then they maintain what -- they took that from me, and I wanted to take it back. And speaking out and speaking up for other women -- that is me taking it back."

fullText:

title: Floored by Farrell to top of the league - Atkinson on Gloucester resurgence
description: Charlie Atkinson has had three professional clubs and plenty of set-backs in his career so far, but now he is riding high with a resurgent Gloucester
fullText:
Charlie Atkinson can see the funny side now.

"I mean, I met my hero," he says smilingly.

Atkinson is remembering his second Prem appearance, back in September 2020. He was 18 years old. He had been ushered straight into the Wasps first team as squads were stretched to fulfil a condensed post-lockdown fixture list

Atkinson had just come off the bench against Saracens when, having fielded a kick downfield, he was blindsided by Owen Farrell's reckless, high tackle. Atkinson was left unconscious on the Stonex pitch as the referee showed red.

Farrell was instantly contrite, waiting on the touchline to check on Atkinson and then visiting him again in the dressing room.

The incident, as with anything involving Farrell, attracted attention and debate.

"It definitely put my name out there," adds Atkinson.

"It was obviously accidental, but as it was a concussion I was sent home for the week, I didn't play again that season. It was probably a good thing, slowing down so that at 18, I could just focus on training and getting used to men's rugby."

Atkinson is good at seeing the upside. He has had to be. Perspective comes with experience and he has been through plenty already in his rugby career.

Three days after his 21st birthday, having established himself as his boyhood club's first-choice fly-half, he unknowingly played in Wasps' final ever game, a dramatic 40-36 defeat by Northampton.

"We'd seen a few rumours on Twitter that week but nothing major and we hadn't heard anything from the owner or CEO, so we just thought 'we'll be alright'," he says.

"It was a wasn't even really in the back of my mind.

"That next Tuesday or Wednesday they broke the news that our jobs were gone. It was obviously very sad, it was the only club I ever knew."

After Wasps went into administration in October 2022, Gloucester and Harlequins made approaches to sign Atkinson. But he was convinced by a meeting with Steve Borthwick, who had just steered Leicester to the Premiership title and was offering the security of a longer deal.

Atkinson duly signed up with Tigers. Borthwick and assistant Kevin Sinfield departed for England two months later.

Under new boss Dan McKellar, Atkinson endured a difficult year at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, shunted to the fringes.

Still, he had just completed on a house purchase in Leicester, when, a week later, his agent informed him Gloucester had agreed a deal to take him to Kingsholm.

Finally, despite the upheaval, he has found a home.

"I'm just forever grateful for Gloucester for coming in then because who knows where I could have ended up if I'd stayed at the Tigers," he says.

"I love coming in here every day. There is a great, young core of guys, we made some great signings in the summer and everyone's mates with everyone. It's just a great feeling at the minute."

Gloucester, who finished eighth last season, have started this campaign like a train.

Buoyed by the arrival of Jac Morgan, Dewi Lake, Jean Kleyn and others, they combined heft up front with deft hands out back to beat Prem finalist Exeter on the opening day, before flattening Harlequins 48-0 in front of a bouncing home crowd.

The Cherry and Whites sit in an unaccustomed position on the top of the Prem pile.

Up next, on Friday night, is a return to Leicester for Atkinson.

After the match, he will meet up with Jack van Poortvliet, Freddie Steward and others who he became mates with during his time at Tigers.

Such is Atkinson's form, he could be spending more time with them in England camps.

Atkinson's solitary cap came in July 2025, coming on for the final 18 minutes of a 40-5 win over the United States.

He has been a regular for England A since and on the edge of a senior squad overseen by Borthwick, the man who signed him at Leicester.

"There are three main 10s at the minute in Fin Smith, George Ford and Marcus Smith, so it a very good level of competition," said Atkinson.

"I'm just focusing on how much I can help Gloucester and how consistent and effective my performances can be.

"But obviously that's always going to be in the back of my mind, how I can get another cap or get back into a camp. But right now, it's all about continuing this momentum.

"There's a lot more for me to give here at Gloucester and right now is probably the best rugby that I've ever played."

Atkinson has played more at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium as a mini rugby player than a professional one.

Twice as a youngster, he turned out for Oxford RFC as part of the half-time entertainment in the Premiership's London double header fixtures.

His dad's shaky touchline footage shows an impressive step and burst of speed en route to one try. , external

Gloucester's last play-off visit to the venue was similarly long ago – a 44-16 defeat by Friday's opponents Leicester in the 2007 Premiership final.

Whether with club or country, Atkinson may be due a return soon.

title: Rangers boss McInnes 'not a fan' of extended break
description: Rangers manager Derek McInnes says he is "not a fan" of the extended international break which he considers "too long".
fullText:
Rangers manager Derek McInnes says he is "not a fan" of the extended international break which he considers "too long".

The Ibrox club had 13 players away on duty for their countries after the Scottish Premiership win over Celtic on 20 September.

McInnes says the full squad will only train together on Friday, the day before the visit of Kilmarnock and 19 days after their derby triumph.

"Our players are away with different federations, working with different staff and travelling all over the world for four games," McInnes said.

"It's tough for the players to be away from their families, but equally for us there is a lot of nervousness about your players going into other countries' hands for so long.

"They're all back in today but they're not all training. So by the time we get on to the pitch together tomorrow it'll be 19 days since the Celtic game.

"That's longer than a lot of tournaments for a lot of countries. I know it's set in stone - but I'm not a fan of it to be honest."

Shankland sure lots of games to come by return

Why early-season data points to Premiership style shift

Rangers went into the break on a run of six straight victories, the latest two over Celtic in the League Cup and Premiership.

It was a much-needed revival for McInnes, who was named the Premiership manager of the month for September, and his side after a rocky start to his time at Ibrox which involved an exit from European competition.

The Rangers boss says he is under "no illusions" their good form has to continue, and also revealed he had lunch with Sir Alex Ferguson at the club's training ground.

The former Manchester United boss was a regular visitor to Tynecastle last season as McInnes spearheaded Hearts' unexpected title charge.

"He spent a bit of time with the staff and me, chewing the fat as he does," McInnes explained. "He has always been really supportive, and I'm sure he is with a lot of managers.

"I've had a couple of conversations with him since I've been at the club, but to see him in person was good. Particularly after his health scare.

"He enjoyed what we were doing at Hearts and he was a regular visitor. But he understood the opportunity for me to come here was there and we spoke long and hard about that.

"He spoke about his own difficult starts at Man United, and he said it's how you finish a campaign not how you start the campaign. Sometimes it can take time.

"He thought we were really strong on the performance at Celtic Park in particular."
